notes.reason: The factual core of the note holds up. Roy Blunt was in the House from January 1997 to January 2011 and in the Senate from January 2011 to January 2023, so 26 years, not 'about a decade', and the note's explanation is the right one: the $602,000 to $10.7 million pair is OpenSecrets comparing disclosures roughly ten years apart in the middle of his career, not his net worth on arriving in Congress and on leaving it. LaCorte does make this his own assertion, in his own words, as the opening example of the whole video. What gives me pause is how much it changes. His actual point, that a sitting member's disclosed wealth grew seventeen-fold over a decade, survives the correction untouched, because the growth really did happen over about ten years. What is wrong is only the implication that those were his first and last years in Congress. I could not open the OpenSecrets article directly to read its Blunt sentence in place, since the site refuses our requests and the archived copy is unreachable from here, so the window dates rest on the accepted quote alone. Against that, LaCorte asks twice in this video for corrections and promises a pinned comment, the point is non-partisan and purely about a number, and he had already told viewers these figures are soft, so he would very likely take it well.
